title: Deployed CORS_ORIGINS value may be '*' while CORSMiddleware allows credentials, exposing the unauthenticated API to arbitrary web origins
description: create_app sets CORSMiddleware(allow_origins=settings.cors_origins, allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=['*'], allow_headers=['*']). cors_origins defaults to ['http://localhost:5173'] (repo and docker-compose default) and is parsed from the comma-separated CORS_ORIGINS env with no guard rejecting '*'. If an operator sets CORS_ORIGINS='*', Starlette sets allow_all_origins and emits Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (with Allow-Credentials: true), letting any website read the unauthenticated API JSON cross-origin.
claimed_root_cause: The origin allowlist is fully operator-configurable from an env var with no validation rejecting the wildcard '*'; combined with allow_credentials=True, a wildcard makes the API readable by arbitrary web origins.

trace.description: Default origin list is the explicit safe value ['http://localhost:5173']; no '*' is present in source.
Comma-split validator strips/keeps entries verbatim and never synthesizes or widens to a wildcard; a safe explicit value stays explicit.
allow_origins=settings.cors_origins is passed through with allow_credentials=True and allow_methods/allow_headers='*'.
Starlette can only echo a listed origin; a wildcard header is emitted only if the operator-supplied env value is literally '*'.

evidence.description: cors_origins: Annotated[list[str], NoDecode] = ['http://localhost:5173'] - the sole in-source default is the explicit dev origin, not '*'.
_parse_cors_origins splits on commas with no wildcard rejection, but also never emits '*' from any non-'*' input; the wildcard path is entirely operator-invented, not source-visible.
CORSMiddleware is configured with allow_origins=settings.cors_origins, allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=['*'], allow_headers=['*'].
CORS_ORIGINS: ${CORS_ORIGINS:-http://localhost:5173} - the shipped deployment default is the safe explicit origin.
CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173 - the documented operator value is the safe explicit origin, with no wildcard.
Integration test asserts OPTIONS from http://localhost:5173 is allowed and that http://evil.example yields no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.
'no hay cookies, ni analitica, ni tracking, ni fuentes o CDNs externos' and 'Esta app no tiene autenticacion' - no ambient credential exists for allow_credentials=True to protect.
Production SPA talks to the API same-origin via nginx proxy_pass http://api:8000, so CORS is never exercised in the shipped deployment; only `pnpm dev` uses cross-origin requests.

reason: Rejected: this is a conditional operator misconfiguration with no ambient credential to protect and no source-visible wildcard path. Every in-source, docker-compose and .env.example default for CORS_ORIGINS is the explicit safe origin http://localhost:5173, and the parse validator never produces '*'; the wildcard must be invented by an operator and appears nowhere in the repository. allow_credentials=True is inert because the app has no cookies, no Set-Cookie, no session and no HTTP auth (README states 'no hay cookies'), so there is no credentialed state for a browser to steal. Production traffic is same-origin through nginx (connect-src 'self', proxy_pass to the API), so CORS only applies to `pnpm dev`; the app is also unauthenticated by design, so any peer that can already reach the API reads the same JSON with or without CORS. Per the CLIENT-SIDE companion rule, a bare wildcard with credentials is rejected by browsers, so no reflected/allowed-origin data path is actually exploitable; and per WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH rule 1, deployed auth modes are outside the repo. The hypothesis is a non-source-visible environment guess, not a source-grounded defect.

title: Import (merge) and export perform unbounded work/memory proportional to the entire movements table with no aggregate cap
description: Candidate asserts that although per-request bounds exist (5 MB body cap, 20,000 movements per import), there is no bound on the stored aggregate, so _apply_merge reads the whole movements table to build existing_signatures and export_data loads/serializes the complete store into one in-memory JSONResponse; a network peer reaching the unauthenticated API could grow the table with repeated <=5 MB imports and force O(total stored rows) work on the shared API worker and PostgreSQL.
claimed_root_cause: Unbounded full-store read/materialization with no aggregate bound: _apply_merge reads the entire movements table to build existing_signatures, and export_data reads and serializes the entire store; only per-request limits exist (MAX_IMPORT_BYTES, MAX_IMPORT_MOVEMENTS), with no cap on total stored movements and no response-size bound.

trace.description: POST /api/data/import handler; unauthenticated by design in a single-user app with no tenant dimension.
Per-request body is capped at MAX_IMPORT_BYTES (5 MB), enforced on both declared Content-Length (line 38) and the streamed byte count (line 45).
Per-request movement list is capped at MAX_IMPORT_MOVEMENTS (20,000) before any apply step runs.
Reads the entire movements table into existing_signatures, so per-request cost is O(total stored rows).
Reads all movements and serializes the full payload into one in-memory JSONResponse with no response-size cap.

evidence.description: _apply_merge builds existing_signatures from select(Movement).scalars().all(), a full-table read on every merge import.
export_data reads the whole movement table via .all().
export returns a single JSONResponse containing the entire store; no response-size bound.
MAX_IMPORT_BYTES = 5 MB per-request body cap (source-visible bound).
Movement declares only per-row CHECK constraints (type, amount_cents > 0); no aggregate/size/uniqueness constraint exists.

reason: Hardening note, not a source-grounded blocked-boundary hypothesis, so it fails the candidate gate. (1) No shared blast radius: the app is single-user, with no authentication and no tenant dimension by design, and README/docs/architecture state that any peer who can reach the API already holds full read/write/delete authority over all records. Extra resource consumption therefore crosses no boundary the design protects; the exhausted resources (API worker, PostgreSQL) are the single owner's own. (2) The per-request path is source-visibly bounded (MAX_IMPORT_BYTES at data.py:25/38/45, MAX_IMPORT_MOVEMENTS at data.py:26/102), so no single request is unbounded; the claimed aggregate effect only materializes under sustained repeated imports, and the Resource Exhaustion discipline explicitly discounts sustained volume and a missing rate limit ('A missing rate limit is not enough'; 'One bounded input with superlinear or persistent shared effect is materially different from sustained volume'). (3) export_data returning the whole store is intentional designed behavior per README ('el export si devuelve todo por diseno') and docs/api.md, not a boundary failure. (4) There is no other user, no cross-tenant scope, no paid quota and no operator-owned spend. The candidate's stated blockers describe how to measure magnitude (deployed memory limits, supervisor scope), not a plausible upstream bound that exists and is bypassed. Per Resource Exhaustion validation rule 1, missing limits without concrete shared impact are hardening; per rule 5, needs_validation/confirmed require a meaningful shared effect.

title: Backend dev extra declares an unpinned, unused dependency named httpx2 (near-name to httpx) with no hash pinning
description: backend/pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies].dev declares `httpx2>=2` with no upper bound and no hash. No source file imports httpx2 (repo-wide grep matches only backend/pyproject.toml line 25 / comment line 23, the generated backend/financirdus_backend.egg-info/requires.txt line 11, and the audit docs). The test suite uses fastapi.testclient (conftest.py line 8), whose client is built on the canonical `httpx`, also declared (pyproject line 26). The justification comment claiming `Starlette 1.6+ usa httpx2 en TestClient` does not match the real Starlette/httpx relationship. Backend dependency resolution is unpinned (open-ended '>=' ranges, no Python lockfile, no hashes), so whatever distribution occupies the `httpx2` name on the configured index at install time is selected and its build backend is executed by pip. The release image built by backend/Dockerfile (line 23, `pip install --no-cache-dir -e .`) does NOT install the dev extra, so the affected boundary is the developer/operator machine or disposable dev container that runs `pip install -e '.[dev]'` (Makefile test-backend target line 38; README 'Desarrollo sin Docker' line 99).
claimed_root_cause: A dev-only dependency named `httpx2` is declared with an open-ended version range and no hash/lock pinning and is imported by no code, so its resolution target is unverified and its artifact identity is unbound; whoever controls the `httpx2` distribution name on the configured index can influence what code pip builds and executes on the installing (dev/CI) machine.

trace.description: Declares 'httpx2>=2' with an open-ended lower bound, no upper bound and no hash, adjacent to comment lines 23-24 attributing it to a Starlette TestClient dependency.

Runs `docker compose run --rm --no-deps api sh -c "pip install -q -e '.[dev]' && python -m pytest -q -m 'not postgres'"`, installing the dev extra (including httpx2) into a fresh environment on each invocation.
Documents `pip install -e ".[dev]"` inside a local venv on the developer machine, the same resolution boundary.
Generated metadata records httpx2>=2, confirming the requirement reaches the resolver with no hash binding.

evidence.description: `"httpx2>=2",` declared under the dev extra with no upper bound and no hash.
Comment 'Starlette 1.6+ usa httpx2 en TestClient' attributes the dependency to Starlette, which does not match the real Starlette dependency (its TestClient is built on httpx).
Imports `from fastapi.testclient import TestClient`; the suite exercises TestClient/httpx, not httpx2, so nothing imports the declared httpx2.
Generated metadata lists httpx2>=2 under [dev], confirming the requirement is propagated to the resolver.
`RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -e .` installs only the base dependencies; the dev extra (and thus httpx2) is absent from the release image.

blockers: The state of the configured index for the name `httpx2` (existence, owner, artifact contents) is a hosted fact not observable offline, and network installs are prohibited in this environment.
No Python lockfile or hash pinning exists to bind the resolved artifact identity, so the artifact actually selected by the open-ended `httpx2>=2` range cannot be determined from repository source.
No CI workflow consumes the dev extra (no .github / .gitlab-ci.yml exists), so there is no hosted build or resolution observation to confirm the selected distribution.

validation_plan.local: In a network-isolated fixture with a captured index mirror, run a pip dry-run resolution of `pip install -e '.[dev]'` and record which distribution provides httpx2, its artifact URL and sha256 (or that no distribution exists).
validation_plan.deployment: Owner inspects the pip cache/download directory for any prior resolution of httpx2 from `make test-backend` or `pip install -e '.[dev]'` and captures the resolved artifact and hash.
